description: Dense trending signals for agentic web search. Ranked by velocity.

ranking.note: Higher velocity = faster-growing attention, not higher absolute volume

items.title: DeepSeek V4 Flash launches free tier
items.summary: DeepSeek released V4 Flash with a free tier: 50 req/day, 284B MoE (13B active), 1M context, MIT license. Dev community reaction overwhelmingly positive. Cost comparison: $0.14/$0.28 vs GPT-5.6 Sol at $5/$15 per M tokens (36x cheaper).
items.why_it_matters: First top-tier coding model with a genuinely usable free tier. Changes the economics for indie devs and small teams.

items.title: Claude Code 3.0 ships with multi-agent orchestration and worktree isolation
items.summary: Anthropic's CLI agent tool adds native multi-agent workflows, git worktree isolation, and a structured review panel. Early adopters report 3-5x productivity gains on complex refactors and migrations. Built-in token-spike circuit breaker and liveness-aware sweep.
items.why_it_matters: Production-grade multi-agent orchestration in a CLI tool, not just a cloud API. Shift from AI-as-autocomplete to AI-as-foreman.

items.title: Cloudflare Workers adds native Python via Pyodide
items.summary: Python now runs natively in Workers via Pyodide: sub-50ms cold starts, native bindings to KV/R2/D1/Queues. No transpilation step needed; import standard library modules directly.
items.why_it_matters: JavaScript's monopoly on edge compute ends. Python's ML/data ecosystem now runs at the edge.

items.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol priced 36x higher than DeepSeek Flash, benchmarks show marginal gap
items.summary: GPT-5.6 Sol ships with improved reasoning at $5/$15 per M tokens. Independent benchmarks show only 3-5% quality gap vs DeepSeek V4 Flash ($0.14/$0.28). Pricing pressure mounts as open-weight alternatives close the gap.
items.why_it_matters: LLM pricing is no longer a moat. The cost-quality frontier is being rewritten by open-weight models.

items.title: Next.js 16 stable — Turbopack default, RSC by default, PPR GA
items.summary: Next.js 16: Turbopack is now the default bundler (10x faster HMR), React Server Components enabled by default, Partial Prerendering reaches GA. Migration guide covers breaking changes from 14/15.
items.why_it_matters: The React ecosystem's new default. Every Next.js project upgrading this quarter hits these changes.

items.title: Aider v0.80 adds multi-model routing, cuts AI coding costs 60-80%
items.summary: Aider now auto-routes by task complexity: simple edits use cheap models, architecture decisions use Claude Opus. One API key, automatic switching. Users report 60-80% cost reduction with no quality loss.
items.why_it_matters: AI coding tooling is converging on smart routing as the default pattern. Single-model workflows are becoming legacy.

items.title: Zustand v5 — 40% smaller bundle, React 19 optimized
items.summary: Zustand v5 drops to 1.1 kB gzipped, fixes the long-standing stale-snapshot warnings, adds first-class TanStack Query integration. Migration from v4 is a single import change for most users.
items.why_it_matters: The most-used React state library gets lighter and fixes its most-Googled bug.

items.title: EU AI Act enforcement begins — first GPAI compliance deadline hits
items.summary: First EU AI Act enforcement milestone now active. GPAI providers must document training data, implement watermarking, publish energy reports. Fines up to 3% of global turnover.
items.why_it_matters: The first major AI regulation with real enforcement teeth. Every model provider shipping to EU users is affected.

items.title: Bun 2.0 lands Windows support, 98% Node.js compat, 2x faster installs
items.summary: Bun 2.0 adds full Windows support (x64 + ARM), Node.js compatibility hits 98% (passes Node's own test suite), install speed doubles. Now a viable drop-in replacement for most Node projects.
items.why_it_matters: Cross-platform maturity makes Bun a real production option, not just a fast toy.

items.title: Tesla Optimus Gen-3 walks untethered outdoors — on-board inference at 50Hz
items.summary: Optimus Gen-3 demonstrated untethered outdoor walking on uneven terrain. Full control stack (perception, planning, actuation) runs on-board at 50 Hz with no cloud offload. Manufacturing pilot begins Q4 2026.
items.why_it_matters: Humanoid robots moving from lab demos to real-world locomotion. On-board inference at 50 Hz is the hardware story.
